comment: Parity corpus for the audience helper (RDR-259 Decisions 1-4, 7 and 11; nexus-sby49.8). Each row lays out a tree under a tmp dir and names the user settings file and the account home. payload is a dict whose cwd is relative to tmp (raw_cwd: taken as written), or null (not a dict), or {} (no cwd). Layout kinds: dir; file (c as text, or bytes_b64 for raw bytes; pad_to appends spaces up to that many bytes); symlink or link (t, relative to tmp); fifo (posix only); rm (deletes a file); git (dir, args: runs git in tmp/dir with no global or system config). home_files use the same kinds, relative to the account home. user is null, an object (written as JSON), a raw string, or "dir" (a directory in its place). expect lists only the fields that differ from defaults; a listed field replaces the default whole. Compared fields: guard_mode, project, user, telemetry, t1_nudge, advice_blocked, brief_questions, integration_branch and problems (sorted [file, key] pairs); remote_test_hosts when a row lists it. Flags: head (readers called with head=True), needs_git (skipped without git on PATH), posix_only, env_project_dir (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, relative to tmp), no_home (no account home), prev_release false (the previous release's helper cannot know the row, or answers it differently on purpose), covers (the Decision 4 and related cases the row exercises). Expectations were derived by hand from the RDR, not taken from running a reader.
